analysis.title: Lyft Inc. (LYFT) Q3'26 Review: Solid Execution Against Strategic Growth Priorities Anchored Around Premiumization, Market Expansion & Autonomous Vehicles
key_insights: GS reiterates Buy on LYFT and lowers the 12-month price target to $20 from $22, implying 12.1% upside from the $17.84 price (5 Nov 2026 close).
Q3'26 Adj. EBITDA of $204mm beat GS ($191mm) by 7% and consensus ($193mm) by 6%, driven by continued cost discipline. Adj. EBITDA margin was 3.6% of gross bookings vs 3.4% for both GS and consensus.
Revenue of $1,822mm missed GS ($1,936mm) by 6% and consensus ($1,920mm) by 5%. Take rate was 32.4% vs 34.3% GS and 34.2% consensus, a gap of about 180 bps.

Gross bookings of $5,617mm were 1% below GS ($5,651mm) and in line with consensus ($5,610mm). Rides of 273.5mm were 1% below both GS and consensus. Active riders of 31.6mm were 3% below GS and 1% below consensus.

Management said North America Rides growth accelerated for the second consecutive quarter and expects it to accelerate again in Q4. Cited drivers are core and low-scale markets, driver supply, partnerships and tailwinds from insurance policy reform.
Premium rides continue to grow double digits YoY. Management plans to launch a chauffeur brand, Alcove, in 2027 aimed at business travel and higher-value customers.
Lyft announced Lyft Go, a combined rideshare and delivery membership program in partnership with DASH, aimed at raising frequency through more affordable rideshare options.
AVs are framed as a TAM-expansion opportunity. Results in Nashville (with Waymo) were solid, and management expects to bring the same operating model to Europe.

International trends were positive: organic growth in rides, active riders and gross bookings across Europe, and growing adoption of cross-border features including ride hailing on the Lyft app in Europe.

Negatives: Q3 Sales & Marketing expense came in above GS on growth investments. The October insurance renewal is expected to modestly raise Q4 insurance costs vs Q3. Investments in international expansion and AVs may weigh on near-term margins.
Q4'26 estimate changes: gross bookings $5.92bn (from $5.75bn), revenue $1.84bn (from $1.98bn), Adj. EBITDA $203mm (from $197mm), GAAP EPS $0.28 (from $0.21).

2027 estimate changes: gross bookings $24.66bn (unchanged), revenue $8.03bn (from $8.36bn), Adj. EBITDA $840mm (from $879mm), GAAP EPS $1.07 (from $1.04). The 2028 Adj. EBITDA estimate falls to $990mm from $1,062mm.

Valuation: the $20 target blends 10.0x EV/GAAP EBITDA on NTM+1 estimates (from 13.0x) with a modified DCF at 6.5x EV/FCF-SBC on NTM+4 estimates discounted 3 years at 12%. Shares trade at about 8x equity value / 2027 FCF-SBC on GS estimates.
Near-term investor focus is the sustainability of mobility growth, the balance of growth investment vs margin, and the free cash flow profile.

market_movers.rationale: Price target cut to $20 from $22 on lower forward operating estimates and a lower EBITDA multiple (10.0x from 13.0x). GS sees attractive valuation at about 8x equity value / 2027 FCF-SBC.

LYFT Q3'26 reported revenue $1,822mm vs GS est $1,936mm and consensus est $1,920mm.

LYFT Q3'26 reported GBs per ride $20.54 vs GS est $20.46 and consensus est $20.39. Revenue per active rider $57.65 vs GS est $59.16 and consensus est $60.08.
GS Q4'26 estimates (new): gross bookings $5.92bn, revenue $1.84bn, Adj. EBITDA $203mm, GAAP EPS $0.28 (old: $5.75bn, $1.98bn, $197mm, $0.21).
GS 2029 estimates: gross bookings $29.6bn (from $30.5bn), revenue $9.64bn (from $10.33bn), Adj. EBITDA $1,150mm (from $1,264mm), GAAP EPS $1.66 (from $1.73).
risk_factors: Active rider growth or frequency below forecasts, including market share loss or slower consumer adoption of mobility.
Unfavorable changes in consumer behavior, including AV adoption away from LYFT, work from home, office commute and airport travel.
Higher insurance costs affecting unit economics.
Macro volatility and investor risk appetite for growth stocks.
